limitations: Components are recognised from the markup. No figure here is a component’s energy: Firefox’s power counters cover whole processes. Whether changing a component saves energy is for a measured comparison (compare), run with and without the change.

Stylesheets, web fonts and CSS background images are not tied to components. Scripts are tied to one only when the element that loads them sits inside it; bundled and global scripts stay unattributed.
Firefox CPU categories are page-level. web-energy diagnose <url> shows them for one representative page.
At most 24 occurrences are recorded per page (the largest, plus smaller ones holding media or animations); counts and sizes cover every occurrence.

Lighthouse evidence comes from Chromium under throttling, a different browser and boundary from the Firefox measurement. It says where Chromium spent main-thread time or found a problem, not what Firefox used.

order: evidence: a structural fact and a Lighthouse finding, then a Lighthouse finding, then a structural fact
workload: elements, or Chromium main-thread time for scripts

remediation.title: Load embeds on interaction
remediation.action: Replace the iframe with a static facade (image and button) and load the embed when someone activates it; otherwise loading="lazy".
remediation.rationale: Each iframe is another document with its own scripts, style and layout; third-party embeds often load far more than they show.
remediation.verify: Compare the page with the facade and with the live embed. Measure it with `web-energy experiment --from <result.json> --item <n>` (interleaved, 10 or more runs per side) on a machine that measures energy, or `web-energy compare` between two builds.

remediation.title: Reserve space so nothing shifts
remediation.action: Give images and embeds width and height (or aspect-ratio), and reserve room for content that arrives later.
remediation.rationale: A layout shift is a relayout and repaint of everything below it, and moves content under the reader.
remediation.verify: Check the layout-shift findings disappear in a fresh Lighthouse run; measure with compare if the shift repeats.

remediation.title: Lazy-load images below the first screen
remediation.action: Add loading="lazy" (and decoding="async") to images below the first screen. Never to the LCP image.
remediation.rationale: Images nobody scrolls to are still downloaded and decoded at load: transfer, decode and memory for nothing.
remediation.verify: Compare the page load with and without loading="lazy". Measure it with `web-energy experiment --from <result.json> --item <n>` (interleaved, 10 or more runs per side) on a machine that measures energy, or `web-energy compare` between two builds.

remediation.title: Render fewer elements
remediation.action: Paginate or virtualise long lists, render menus and other hidden content on demand rather than on every page, and remove wrappers that exist only for styling.
remediation.rationale: Every element is re-examined on style recalculation and layout, so a large subtree costs work on load and on every later change.
remediation.verify: Compare the template with the smaller markup (a paginated or virtualised variant). Measure it with `web-energy experiment --from <result.json> --item <n>` (interleaved, 10 or more runs per side) on a machine that measures energy, or `web-energy compare` between two builds.

remediation.title: Reserve space so nothing shifts
remediation.action: Give images and embeds width and height (or aspect-ratio), and reserve room for content that arrives later.
remediation.rationale: A layout shift is a relayout and repaint of everything below it, and moves content under the reader.
remediation.verify: Check the layout-shift findings disappear in a fresh Lighthouse run; measure with compare if the shift repeats.

remediation.title: Serve images at the size shown
remediation.action: Use srcset and sizes, and a modern format, so no image is decoded at many times its displayed size.
remediation.rationale: Images are decoded at natural size whatever CSS does, so an oversized image costs CPU and memory as well as bytes.
remediation.verify: Compare transfer and decode before and after; measure with compare for energy.

remediation.title: Render fewer elements
remediation.action: Paginate or virtualise long lists, render menus and other hidden content on demand rather than on every page, and remove wrappers that exist only for styling.
remediation.rationale: Every element is re-examined on style recalculation and layout, so a large subtree costs work on load and on every later change.
remediation.verify: Compare the template with the smaller markup (a paginated or virtualised variant). Measure it with `web-energy experiment --from <result.json> --item <n>` (interleaved, 10 or more runs per side) on a machine that measures energy, or `web-energy compare` between two builds.
